finalText:
I went through all 380 commits and the PR sheet. Most of it really was noise — dependency bumps, internal refactors (renaming types, splitting files, collapsing helpers), and test-only changes. I filtered down to what a user would actually notice and added a `4.2.0` section to CHANGELOG.md, placed above 4.1.0 to keep it newest-first (the placeholder comment at the bottom was stale, so I removed it).

What made the cut:

**Breaking** — an expired token now returns `401` instead of `403`. Worth flagging since clients that branch on status code need updating.

**Added** — webhook delivery retries with backoff (the one real `feat` commit in the whole log).

**Fixed** — 10 items, the biggest being: the database no longer logs full request bodies (a privacy fix), and pagination no longer breaks on a null cursor across four different modules (API, queue, webhooks, database) — that one showed up as four separate near-identical commits, so I collapsed it into one bullet rather than listing it four times. Same treatment for the "empty allowlist" crash, which also recurred across three modules.

One thing worth flagging: several fix titles repeated verbatim across unrelated modules and even within the same module multiple times (e.g., "drop the duplicate header" fixed three separate times in `core` alone). I read that as the same class of bug recurring in parallel codepaths rather than a regression loop, and wrote one bullet per bug class — but if any of those were actually distinct incidents worth calling out separately, let me know and I'll split them.
